title: What are the corresponding angles of parallel lines?
description: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal and the angle a is sixty five degrees. The board finds b, then the angle next to a, and lists the four pairs of corresponding angles. Keeko doubts that b is the angle next to a.
teaching_notes: One idea: corresponding angles of parallel lines are equal, so b matches a and the other pairs follow from the linear pair. Watch for students who give b the measure of the angle next to a.

source: Lines l and m are parallel, with arrow marks, and t crosses both. The angle a at l is 65°, and b is its corresponding angle at m. Find b and the other three pairs of corresponding angles.
video_script.why: The child uses equal corresponding angles of parallel lines to find b and the other pairs.
video_script.substitution: The book's own result: corresponding angles formed by a transversal on parallel lines are always equal.
video_script.anchor: Two parallel lines l and m with arrow marks, crossed by a line t, with the angle a of sixty five degrees at l and the angle b at m in the same corner.
video_script.wrong_answer: b is one hundred and fifteen degrees
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks b is next to a, so b must be the other angle of the linear pair.
video_script.payoff_line: The angle b is sixty five degrees.

final_answer.value: b = 65°; the four pairs of corresponding angles are 65°, 65°, 115° and 115°
final_answer.spoken: b is sixty five degrees, and the four pairs of corresponding angles are sixty five, sixty five, one hundred and fifteen and one hundred and fifteen degrees

hold_back: b = 65°; the four pairs of corresponding angles are 65°, 65°, 115° and 115°
maths_rules: corresponding angles of parallel lines are equal, so b = 65
the angle next to a on the straight line is 180 - 65 = 115, and its corresponding angle is also 115
of the four pairs of corresponding angles, two pairs are 65 and two pairs are 115
each pair is equal because the lines are parallel
the slip: b is in the same corner as a, at the other line, so b is not next to a
video_script.design: One figure stays on the stage with the arrow marks on the two lines. The pairs of corresponding angles light up two at a time in the same colour.

<bookmark mark='m2'/>A line t crosses both of them. The angle eigh at the first line is sixty five degrees.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A line that crosses two other lines is called a transversal.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Angles in the same corner at the two crossings are called corresponding angles.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>When the two lines are parallel, the corresponding angles are always equal.

<bookmark mark='m2'/>One hundred and eighty take away sixty five is one hundred and fifteen.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Its corresponding angle is also one hundred and fifteen degrees.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks b is one hundred and fifteen degrees, because b is next to eigh.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But b is not next to eigh. It is in the same corner, at the other line.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Its measure must match the measure of eigh.
